1. The point-support geometric decoder proof passes

The proposed neutralization algorithm can use exact local GF(2) Gaussian elimination without assuming TQO2 or a free local-completion oracle.

The essential invariant is that each successful correction deletes detector positions and creates none. Corrections are assigned to a true peel by the detector subset they remove, regardless of whether their physical supports overlap another correction. At the peel’s scale, its true fault restriction plus earlier assigned corrections is an explicit local solution. Thus premature partial corrections do not invalidate the peeling argument.

With the measured terminal boundary below, every residual piece is a zero-syndrome Pauli supported on fewer than $d_N$ qubits and hence a stabilizer. No locally supported expression in stabilizer generators is needed.

$$z=Hm+y_L^A+y_L^B.$$

$$HR(f)=0,\qquad
R(f)=\sum_t f^A_{\mathrm{data},t}
+\sum_t f^B_{\mathrm{data},t}+f_{\mathrm{terminal}}.$$

If the decoder solves $A_{\mathrm{det}}x=d_{\mathrm{actual}}$, then

$$m'=m+R(x)\in\ker H.$$

Its logical Pauli class gives the Bell frame. Small residual zero-detector pieces cannot change that class.
